source.title: Outlier Gradient Analysis: Efficiently Improving Deep Learning Model Performance via Hessian-Free Influence Functions
source.authors: Anshuman Chhabra; Bo Li; Jian Chen; Prasant Mohapatra; Hong-Fu Liu

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper, including appendices. The title in the supplied metadata differs from the title printed in the paper; no text appears cut off.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports test accuracy after removing samples identified as detrimental or mislabeled, but it does not test the catalog’s memorization/generalization claims: it uses neither random-label memorization nor the memorized-example criterion in V8.
record.gate_note: The paper's results concern detecting and trimming mislabeled or detrimental training samples and resulting test accuracy. Those interventions are adjacent to, but do not test, the claim versions. Rows are recorded as findings about the claim's subject with versions ["none"]. Cited results from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates gradient-based detection and removal of detrimental or mislabeled training samples. It does not select examples by V8's memorization criterion or compare their removal with equally sized random removals. Its other experiments do not manipulate or measure the comparisons specified in V1–V7. Citing Feldman and Zhang does not constitute testing V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that outlier-gradient analysis provides an efficient Hessian-free approach to detrimental-sample identification, with competitive detection and post-trimming performance in vision and NLP, and influential-class identification in LLMs. Their conclusion concerns their method's utility, not any of V1–V8.
record.recipe_differences: The paper's method detects outlying training gradients and trims samples to improve performance; it does not study random-label memorization, standard training generalization, or the interventions in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper varies dataset and noise setting, trimming budget, outlier method, and model architecture. It reports different test accuracies across these settings; it does not analyze their effects on a generalization gap.

fits_no_version.finding: Half-moons iForest trimming raises test accuracy from 90% to 96%, whereas L1 and L2 trimming lower it to 87%. Reported vision-model trimming results improve held-out accuracy over the full-data baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Removing gradient outliers from noisy-label training data can improve held-out performance, with outcomes depending on the detection method and setting.

fits_no_version.finding: For RoBERTa data selection, the authors report the best test results on QNLI, SST2, and QQP, and performance comparable to Self-LiSSA on MRPC.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient-outlier data selection can compete with influence-based selection methods when fine-tuning on noisy binary text-classification datasets.

record.problems: The paper studies noisy-label detection and data selection rather than the claim's generalization-gap variables or memorization criteria. The main CIFAR-10N/CIFAR-100N table omits standard deviations, which are supplied in Appendix C.1. The ImageNet experiment is explicitly described as limited; Table 10 gives no uncertainty values.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were extracted for versions V1–V8 because the study does not test those version-specific behaviors. Other baseline-method results and data-selection results shown only as plots were left out because they do not test a claim version; Figure 3 has no readable numeric values in the supplied text.

untested.parts: Coexistence of near-perfect fixed random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe, including chance-level random-label held-out accuracy.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity or transferred initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization and dependence on tuning, weight decay, or optimizer switching.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover held-out performance.
Held-out effects of adding or removing dropout, including interactions with dataset size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness ranking generalization gaps and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing examples selected by their inclusion's effect on predicting their own labels, compared with removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Held-out accuracy is relevant to several claim versions; failure to report a train–test gap alone does not exclude those versions. Here exclusion rests on the missing version-specific interventions and comparisons. States marked cannot_determine indicate that these rows cannot establish a version's effect, not that their reported accuracy changes are unreadable.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy on natural labels under the same standard training recipe.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and corresponding test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and effects of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under different tuning or decay choices.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Sharpness or other measured properties tracking the train–test generalization gap.
Removing examples selected by how much their inclusion raises the chance of predicting their own label correctly.

rows.subject: Multilayer Perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Trim predicted outlier samples using outlier-gradient iForest, then retrain; paper reports the test classification performance.
rows.note: The result concerns removal of detected mislabeled samples, not memorized examples or a train–test error gap.
rows.check: The 90% to 96% result is correct, but it measures the proposed trimming method's performance, not any claim version; exclude from claim-evidence rows.
